text: Kafka stores bytes, nothing more. It never parses or validates a message's shape — producer and consumer have to independently agree on a serialization format.
JSON is the easy first choice, but nothing enforces a shape. A producer can rename a field, Kafka accepts it either way, and the consumer's code breaks silently.
Avro flips the order — a schema defining field names and types comes first, and every message is validated against it, more compactly than JSON.
Confluent Cloud rejecting an Avro schema change that would have broken existing consumers, before the producer is ever allowed to register it.
JSON is easy but enforces nothing; Avro enforces a shape up front. Next up: Chapter 3, starting with replication and fault tolerance.
